shared_elements: low-relief carving on the flat/rounded front face
horizontal band of repeated pattern crossing the body
raised horizontal ridge or band separating registers
stacked zones/registers of decoration from top to bottom
upper zone with a row of repeated rounded elements
justification: Both are tall free-standing stone blocks whose front face is divided into stacked zones by a horizontal patterned band, with rounded/disc-like elements repeated in the upper zone and further motifs below — a genuinely comparable registered scheme on a monolith. The decisive difference is content and handling: B carries clearly legible profile animals (quadrupeds and birds) in crisp, shallow, pale-stone relief, while A's motifs are abstract discs, ridges and curved arcs in thick, worn, dark-stone modelling on what reads as a body with a head, so nothing suggests a shared hand or repertoire.
